pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: Filesystem drop handling now supports navigator nodes that cannot provide a local Path but can provide an InputStream, including Eclipse IFile-backed DBNResource nodes. Such content is copied into the target folder under the node display name, replacing an existing target. Path existence handling also now skips only paths known not to exist rather than every path for which existence cannot be confirmed.

behavior_changes.description: Callers adapting a DBNResource backed by an Eclipse IFile to InputStream can now receive the file contents. If Eclipse cannot provide the contents, adaptation now fails with an unchecked RuntimeException.
evidence: The new adapter branch applies only to InputStream requests for IFile resources.
CoreException is logged and wrapped as RuntimeException.

behavior_changes.description: Dropping a node without a Path can now copy content supplied through its InputStream adapter into the destination folder. The target name is the node display name, and an existing same-named target is replaced; this fallback copies rather than moving or deleting the source.
evidence: A null Path now triggers an InputStream adapter lookup instead of immediate skipping.
The fallback resolves the node display name beneath the destination folder and uses REPLACE_EXISTING when the target exists.

behavior_changes.description: For a non-null source Path, the drop operation now skips it only when the filesystem positively reports that it does not exist. A path whose existence is indeterminate, such as because of access or I/O conditions, can proceed into the existing copy/move handling instead of being discarded at this check.
evidence: The existence guard now uses Files.notExists rather than negating Files.exists.

important_symbols.reason: This is the central behavior change: it introduces the stream-backed fallback and changes the source-path existence decision used during drop processing.
This new helper determines target path construction, collision replacement, and stream-copy behavior.
This supplies the new InputStream capability for Eclipse IFile resources and defines its failure behavior.

investigation_hints.description: Trace which drag/drop, paste, import, or navigator actions call dropNodes and what move-versus-copy expectations they impose on Path-less nodes.

local_risks.description: The newly obtained InputStream is not closed in the shown fallback or helper. If the adapter contract makes the consumer responsible for closing it, repeated copies can retain file descriptors or workspace resources.

If node display names are not guaranteed to be single safe filename components, resolving them directly can select a nested, parent-relative, or absolute location rather than a file strictly inside the drop folder. Because existing targets are replaced, this could overwrite an unintended file.

The stream-backed branch replaces an existing same-named target without any conflict decision visible here. Distinct source nodes sharing a display name, or an accidental collision with destination content, can therefore lose the prior target contents.
